definition: Chronically suicidal describes a person who has persistent or recurring suicidal behaviour over time, rather than a brief or isolated episode. In the source, it is discussed alongside self-harm behaviour as a long-standing clinical problem.

reasons: The packet supports only that the phrase appears in a discussion of DBT as a treatment for “chronically suicidal and/or self-harm behaviour” in patients with borderline personality disorder; it does not define the term as persistent or recurring suicidal behaviour over time.
The statement that it is “discussed alongside self-harm behaviour as a long-standing clinical problem” adds an unsupported generalization not present in the source.
The packet uses the phrase “chronically suicidal” but does not define it (e.g., it does not explicitly state that it means persistent or recurring over time rather than a brief/isolated episode).

The definition’s claim that it is “discussed alongside self-harm behaviour as a long-standing clinical problem” is only partially supported: the packet pairs “chronically suicidal and/or self-harm behaviour,” but it does not explicitly describe either as “long-standing” or provide time-based wording for the term itself.
